facts.raw_span: 2-year history of progressively worsening fever
weight loss, night sweats, and a dry cough
chronic lower back pain without neurologic deficits
painful nonhealing ulcer on his right hallux
two sputum GeneXpert tests at local clinics, both negative
Hemoglobin 10.9 g/dL
ESR >130 mm/hr
CRP 113 mg/L
induced sputum was trace positive for MTB on GeneXpert
biopsy of the toe ulcer showed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with a solitary acid-fast bacillus
Chest radiograph showed bilateral reticular-nodular opacities
MRI of the spine revealed contiguous spondylitis from T6 to T10 with discitis and an epidural/paraspinal collection causing spinal cord compression

concepts.why: The patient has a 2-year history of worsening symptoms, including fever, weight loss, and night sweats, and has tested positive for MTB on GeneXpert, with biopsy of the toe ulcer showing necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with a solitary acid-fast bacillus.

The patient has chronic lower back pain and MRI of the spine revealed contiguous spondylitis from T6 to T10 with discitis and an epidural/paraspinal collection causing spinal cord compression, consistent with Pott's disease.

The patient has a painful nonhealing ulcer on his right hallux and biopsy of the toe ulcer showed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with a solitary acid-fast bacillus, and has abnormal urine tests, consistent with renal tuberculosis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms and test results, including a trace positive GeneXpert test, necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with acid-fast bacillus in the toe ulcer, and bilateral reticular-nodular opacities on chest radiograph, are consistent with tuberculosis. Pott's disease is a subtype of tuberculosis that affects the spine, and while the patient has spinal involvement, the broader diagnosis of tuberculosis better explains the full range of symptoms and findings.
